source_en: Client meeting, downtown finance office.
Home after late-night bookkeeping.
Delivering ledgers to the treasury district.
Collecting payments from an associate.
Meeting clients I won't name.
Checking secured deposits. Things deteriorate.
Closing accounts before the last deadline.
Final settlement papers for a client.
Home near the station. Alone, deliberately.
Sunday lunch with my parents.
Typing course. Numbers confuse me.
My husband's birthday, with his family.
Picking my children up from school.
Ask anything. I have nothing to hide.
Back to my village. Never lived here.
Home to my family. Mother's waiting up.
Settling Father's estate with my brothers.
Opening my flat to evacuated families.
Don't mind the mask. Old scars. Nothing interesting.
You have a very serious expression. I find that attractive.
Still the same face at this window. I appreciate consistency.
I can make this quick. We both have long days ahead.
These last few days, I find myself almost sentimental.
I won't ask about your rules. You don't ask about mine.
My papers are ready. I was here yesterday. Remember?
The mask is part of my face. It stays.
I have everything you need. You can ask me things.
I came prepared. I always come prepared for you.
I know what you need to see. Look closer.
The mask does not come off. You already know why.
Good instincts, officer. I will remember that.
You make this easier every time. I appreciate that.
Smooth as always. Until the next one.
I will need to contact someone. One moment.
You will hear from people I know. I say that calmly.
The mask… stays on… even now…
You could have… just looked away…
Where are you coming from?
A client near the station. Ledgers. Nothing to interest you.
Collecting payments. People are slow this season. I am patient. Mostly.
Closing accounts before the deadline. Very little left to close.
My mother's flat in Rustavi. She cooks for me every Sunday.
The airport. I fly in from Moscow. I don't live here.
The textile factory, night shift. Numbers were never my talent.
I was already here. Before you sat down.
The same place I always come from. Behind you.
I don't remember where. But I arrived. I always arrive.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
Nothing. The mask covers old scars, not fever. Stop staring.
Tired. I stopped counting sleepless hours. Discuss it privately?
I don't feel much lately. I've started calling that steady.
Nothing. The mask is for show. At home, it's off.
None. My husband would notice. He notices everything about me.
Perfect health. No scars under the mask. Shall I?
No. Ask again. The answer will still be no.
I don't think so. The skin underneath disagrees.
I can't tell anymore. The mask feels for me.
You keep staring. Most people have manners.
The family section is blank on purpose. Note it down.
I could make this easier. If you're the right professional.
The mask isn't medical or decorative. It is simply mine.
By now we know each other. Checkpoints do that.
No next of kin to list. That was always deliberate.
